articles.title: Man Arrested at LeBron James' Home on Stalking Charges
articles.summary: A man was arrested Friday night at LeBron James' Brentwood home on stalking charges after security spotted him on cameras around 9 p.m. and called police. The suspect claimed to be James' son; the LAPD confirmed the arrest to ESPN. James was not home — he was playing in Cleveland — and the suspect did not enter the residence. His identity has not been disclosed.

articles.title: Bucks' 1-8 Start Faces a Test Against the Celtics
articles.summary: The Raptors beat the Bucks 121-107 on Friday at Fiserv Forum, Milwaukee's fifth straight loss and its worst start since 1993-94. The 1-8 Bucks host the 7-2 Celtics on Sunday at 8:00 PM ET. Rookie Brayden Burries posted his first career double-double (21 points, 11 rebounds) in the Toronto loss, and Tyler Herro added 23 points and 10 assists.

articles.title: Porzingis Steps Away From Basketball to Prioritize His Health
articles.summary: Kristaps Porzingis announced Friday he is stepping away from basketball to prioritize his health. He has played 0 games for Golden State this season. He did not say retirement — he remains under contract (2 years / $40M re-signed in June). He was diagnosed with POTS in 2025, and ESPN reported Golden State is withholding his $20M salary for not rendering services.

articles.title: Blue Jays Distance Themselves From Santander's Anti-Muslim Posts
articles.summary: After the November 3 elections, Anthony Santander reposted two videos to his Instagram story on Wednesday, November 4 — one saying "America voted for Sharia Last Night!" over an image of Michigan senator-elect Abdul El-Sayed, and another saying "Islam is not peaceful" — and deleted them Thursday morning. The Blue Jays issued a statement saying "Baseball is for everyone" that did not name Santander. No disciplinary action has been announced, and Santander has not apologized publicly.

articles.title: Luka Doncic Scores Season-High 53 as Lakers Beat Blazers 124-118
articles.summary: Luka Doncic scored a season-high 53 points (17/33 FG, 14/18 FT) with 5 rebounds and 5 assists as the Lakers beat the Trail Blazers 124-118 on Friday at Crypto.com Arena, lifting his scoring average to 40.1 points per game. It was his 11th career 50-point game and his fourth straight 40+ game — the first Laker to do that since Kobe Bryant in 2012. His 363 points through 9 games are the most since Wilt Chamberlain in 1962. The Lakers are 8-2.

articles.title: Ronaldo Announces International Retirement After Rift With Coach Jorge Jesus
articles.summary: Cristiano Ronaldo announced his retirement from Portugal duty, effective after the November international break, following a fallout with coach Jorge Jesus. He leaves with 234 caps and 146 goals — both men's international records — and continues his club career at Al-Nassr.

articles.title: Wembanyama Explodes for Career-High 52 in Spurs' 112-111 Win Over Mavericks
articles.summary: Victor Wembanyama poured in a career-high 52 points with 24 rebounds and 8 blocks, hitting the game-winning free throw with 24.2 seconds left as the Spurs edged the Mavericks 112-111 for their sixth straight win.

articles.title: Bo Naylor Testifies He Saw Nothing Unusual in Clase-Ortiz Pitch Case
articles.summary: Former Guardians catcher Bo Naylor testified Thursday in Brooklyn that he noticed nothing unusual about pitches from Emmanuel Clase or Luis Ortiz, who are accused of rigging pitches. Under cross-examination he said he didn't know gamblers could bet on individual pitches until the case arose.

articles.title: Jaguars Rout Shorthanded Ravens 33-10 in Dominant Display
articles.summary: The Jaguars crushed the short-handed Ravens 33-10 for their fifth win in six games. Trevor Lawrence threw for 242 yards and a touchdown, Cam Little kicked four field goals, and Jacksonville's defense forced three turnovers while holding Derrick Henry to 57 yards.

articles.title: MLB Pitch-Rigging Trial Opens as Baseball Faces Integrity Test
articles.summary: The federal trial of Guardians pitchers Emmanuel Clase and Luis Ortiz began Monday in Brooklyn, with both accused of rigging pitches as part of a betting scheme. A major MLB storyline moves from the diamond to the courtroom.
LeBron James leads a 4th quarter comeback.
